_comment: Structural parameters and widths, single source of truth.
tools/gen-params.py emits TWO packages, and the split is the point:
ccv_params_pkg   values that follow from decisions already made
ccv_prov_pkg     placeholders awaiting a per-block session
A skeleton may reference both. Anything referencing ccv_prov_pkg is known
to be unfinished, and making that visible AT EVERY USE SITE is what stops
a placeholder from being believed -- the same argument the fail-open
register makes about mechanisms that produce confident wrong answers.
Provisional names also carry a CCV_P_ prefix, so the signal survives being
`isa` values are NOT ours to sweep: the compiler is already built against
THE ROUND TRIP IS 2 EVERYWHERE, by construction rather than by choice.
Credit depth, rescue depth and drain wait are not three numbers -- they
are that one number under three names, which is why a future non-abutting
interface moves all of them together.

params.name: CCV_WARP_LANES
params.doc: Lanes per warp. A logical GPR holds 32 lanes, one element each, at every chwidth.

params.name: CCV_GPRS
params.doc: Architectural GPRs. 16 x 1024 bit = 2 KB per warp.

params.name: CCV_PREDS
params.source: ISA v1.6 §1 -- provisional pending compiler data; measured pressure 1-2 of 4
params.doc: Logical predicates. A performance parameter, not a structural ceiling.

params.name: CCV_ADDR_BITS
params.doc: Global address width.

params.name: CCV_DATAPATH_BITS
params.doc: Physical datapath width.

params.name: CCV_TIER1_WARPS
params.doc: Tier-1 resident warps, SMT-4 equivalent. Four slots covering a DRAM latency near 1000 cycles requires that demotion happen only on TRUE misses -- demoting on short stalls would need roughly 84 warps to keep 4 slots busy.

params.name: CCV_PARKED_WARPS
params.doc: Warps parked in PCA. 32 total contexts.

params.name: CCV_FETCH_PER_WARP
params.doc: Instructions fetched per warp per cycle, all 4 tier-1 warps in parallel.

params.name: CCV_DECODE_WIDTH
params.doc: Decode output per cycle. Sized for burst absorption ahead of OOE; expected to move once the timing model produces event traces.

params.name: CCV_ISSUE_WIDTH
params.doc: Rename and issue width. The binding width of the machine.

params.name: CCV_ROB_INSTANCES
params.doc: One ROB per tier-1 warp.

params.name: CCV_RETIRE_PER_ROB
params.doc: Retire per ROB per cycle. 8 peak against 4-wide issue.

params.name: CCV_AGU_PIPES
params.doc: Address generation pipes in MIU, sized for 8-bit coalescing.

params.name: CCV_TLB_XLAT_PER_CYCLE
params.doc: TLB translations per cycle on the hit path, no page split.

params.name: CCV_DCACHE_LOOKUPS
params.doc: D-cache lookups per cycle.

params.name: CCV_SPM_BYTES
params.doc: Scratchpad capacity, 128 KB.

params.name: CCV_SPM_BANKS
params.doc: Scratchpad banks, 32 x 32 bits. Bank conflicts are a first-order GEMM effect, which is why the scratchpad is a design block rather than testbench.

params.name: CCV_BARRIER_ENTRIES
params.source: ISA v1.6 §3, Format E -- 6-bit barrier ID
params.doc: Barrier table entries, 4 x 16, epoch-tagged. A §7 formal target.

params.name: CCV_CORE_ID_BITS
params.doc: Up to 4 cores per MLC. Present from day one rather than added when a second core appears, because adding a struct field later regenerates every typedef, header, harness and checker at that boundary.

params.name: CCV_DEMOTION_THRESHOLD
params.doc: Cycles before the CSR-programmable demotion fallback fires. MLC miss is the primary trigger; this is the backstop.

params.name: CCV_MIGRATION_CYCLES
params.doc: Migration transfer, 2 KB at 1024 bits, each way. At one swap per ~125 cycles this uses the single migration path at about 25 percent.

params.name: CCV_NGD_BUDGET
params.source: §2 -- ~1.5 GHz at Vmin 0.55 V on an N3E-class process
params.doc: Normalized gate delay in one cycle. OPEN (§2): whether 25 is the Vmin-corner number or a nominal one. Per-INTERFACE-PATH budgets are assigned once contracts are drawn, not per block.

params.name: CCV_W_WARP_ID
params.doc: Warp id. 32 total warp contexts.

params.name: CCV_W_TIER1_ID
params.doc: Tier-1 slot, which also selects the ROB instance.

params.name: CCV_W_ARCH_REG
params.doc: Architectural GPR index. 16 GPRs (ISA v1.6 §1).

params.name: CCV_W_ARCH_PRED
params.doc: Architectural predicate index. 4 predicates (ISA v1.6 §1). A separate namespace from the GPRs, with its own RAT and count, even while the width happens to be smaller.

params.name: CCV_W_DISP
params.doc: Memory displacement, sign-extended at the AGU. The widest memory-format offset is cas's 16-bit signed field (ISA v1.6 §3); Format D's simm13, D-prime's simm10, the atomics' simm9 and base+index's simm8 all fit. (The compiler had declared cas's offset uimm16, which would have needed 17: compiler F-143, fixed.)

params.name: CCV_W_CTAID
params.doc: srd #1's %ctaid, the flat CTA index within the grid (ISA v1.6 §5.3). Dispatch state, held by RAU and shadowed in OOE, which substitutes it into srd's immediate at issue. It exactly fills CCV_P_W_IMM, so it sets that parameter's floor.

params.name: CCV_W_WARP_IN_CTA
params.doc: A warp's index within its CTA. %ctatid is 10 bits (ISA v1.6 §5.3) and a warp is 32 lanes, so 5. srd #0's warp_base = warp_in_cta << 5 has its low five bits zero, so the lane ORs its hardwired index in without an adder.

params.name: CCV_W_LANE_MASK
params.doc: One bit per lane.

params.name: CCV_W_DATA
params.doc: Full datapath, 32 lanes x 32 bits.

params.name: CCV_W_LANE_DATA
params.doc: Lane datapath.

params.name: CCV_W_CHWIDTH
params.doc: Element width code: 32, 16, 8, 4.

params.name: CCV_W_CORE_ID
params.doc: Up to 4 cores per MLC.

params.name: CCV_W_INSTR
params.doc: Longest instruction form (ISA v1.6: 16/32/48).

params.name: CCV_W_ILEN
params.doc: Instruction length code: three lengths.

params.name: CCV_W_VA
params.doc: Address generation is 64-bit, though the ISA's architectural address is 48.

params.name: CCV_W_SPM_ADDR
params.doc: 128 KB scratchpad.

params.name: CCV_W_SPM_BANK
params.doc: 32 banks.

params.name: CCV_W_SPM_WORD
params.doc: 4 KB per bank, 32-bit words.

params.name: CCV_W_BAR_ENTRY
params.doc: 64 barrier entries.

params.name: CCV_W_BAR_ID
params.doc: 16 barriers per CTA.

params.name: CCV_W_FAULT_CAUSE
params.doc: Fault-model cause set, with headroom.

params.name: CCV_RT_ABUT
params.doc: Flop-to-flop round trip, abutting. TWO EVERYWHERE BY CONSTRUCTION -- flops on both sides with no exceptions, plus abutment, gives exactly this. It is not a per-interface choice, and the three values below are not independent numbers but the same number under different names. Only a non-abutting interface would differ, and none is known to be until floorplan.

params.name: CCV_CREDIT_TURNAROUND
params.doc: What the endpoints add to the round trip before a credit can be spent again: the payload lands one cycle after its valid, the receiver returns the credit the cycle after that, and a credit that arrives is usable the cycle after (channel.h, credit_smoke.sv). So the credit loop is CCV_RT_ABUT + 2 = 4, not the round trip. Rescue depth and drain wait count only in-flight VALIDS and stay equal to the round trip.

params.name: CCV_CREDIT_DEPTH
params.doc: Credits held by a sender, and so the entries a receiver buffers: the CREDIT LOOP, CCV_RT_ABUT + CCV_CREDIT_TURNAROUND, so a channel runs at full bandwidth, one message per slot per cycle, at steady state. It was 2, equal to the round trip on the claim that abutting blocks are never throttled; measured, that runs every slot at half rate (Q-43, decided 2026-09-26: channels always run at full bandwidth). A repeated link's loop is 2N longer, and its depth with it. Proved in tools/check-formal.sh: full rate at this depth, and not at one less.

params.name: CCV_RESCUE_DEPTH
params.doc: Storage a stalling receiver reserves to catch everything already in flight. Equals the round trip: no unwinding, no negative acknowledgement.

params.name: CCV_DRAIN_WAIT
params.doc: Cycles to wait after asserting stall before nothing is in flight. Equals the round trip, which is what lets sleep entry, chwidth change and demotion share one mechanism and one proof.

params.name: CCV_WAKE_LAT
params.doc: Wake latency: round trip plus 2.

params.name: CCV_P_ROB_DEPTH
params.doc: ROB sizing against 4-wide issue.

params.name: CCV_P_W_ROB_TAG
params.doc: Tier-1 id plus ROB depth.

params.name: CCV_P_PHYS_REGS
params.doc: Rename headroom above 16 arch regs per tier-1 warp.

params.name: CCV_P_W_PHYS_REG
params.doc: Follows CCV_P_PHYS_REGS.

params.name: CCV_P_PRED_REGS
params.doc: Predicate file depth.

params.name: CCV_P_MAX_CTA
params.doc: Resident CTAs, bounded by scratchpad allocation.

params.name: CCV_P_W_CTA_SLOT
params.doc: Follows CCV_P_MAX_CTA.

params.name: CCV_P_W_PA
params.doc: Physical address width at the coherent boundary.

params.name: CCV_P_LINE_BYTES
params.doc: Cache line size.

params.name: CCV_P_W_IMM
params.doc: Widest immediate after format decode. Floor 32, set by identity rather than inherited: OOE substitutes srd #1's %ctaid (CCV_W_CTAID, 32) into this field at issue (Q-38), so it cannot shrink below that.

params.name: CCV_P_TIMEOUT_N
params.doc: Outstanding-request timeout for local interfaces. Provisional BY CONSTRUCTION: N cannot be justified before contention data exists, so revising it is an expected Stage 4b output rather than a spec change.

params.name: CCV_P_TIMEOUT_MEM
params.doc: Outstanding-request timeout for the memory path. Must exceed worst-case DRAM latency.

params.name: CCV_W_ASID
params.doc: Address-space id. 256 address spaces before a rollover forces a flush; with one resident context it exists to make switches cheap.

params.name: CCV_W_STATUS
params.doc: Memory completion status: complete, replay, fault. `cause` carries the detail, so this stays at exactly the three outcomes.

params.name: CCV_W_ACCESS_SIZE
params.doc: Cache access size as a CODE -- powers of two up to a line -- not a byte count. Distinct from CCV_W_CHWIDTH, which is the architectural element width one level up.

params.name: CCV_W_CONFLICT_SER
params.doc: Extra cycles an SPM bank conflict cost, bounded by 32 banks with headroom. A per-lane conflict bitmap belongs in a debug trace, not the datapath.

params.name: CCV_W_RETIRED_CNT
params.doc: Retire count since context restore, SATURATING. The progress guard stops caring well before 256, so this is a saturation choice rather than a true maximum.

params.name: CCV_W_CSR
params.doc: CSR-programmed policy value. Thresholds are tuning knobs, so they get the full CSR width rather than a tight fit.

params.name: CCV_P_W_PHYS_PRED
params.doc: Predicate physical register index. The predicate file is a SEPARATE namespace with its own RAT; sharing CCV_P_W_PHYS_REG would recouple two files that were deliberately split.
params.decided_at: Stage 4a -- OOE rename session sizes the predicate RAT

params.name: CCV_P_W_REQ_MIU_SPM
params.doc: req_id on MIU -> SPM: correlates a response with its request. Per hop, never shared across hops, and not rob_tag (one instruction can be several transactions; FET has no ROB tag). Eight outstanding scratchpad accesses: four slots, two deep.
params.decided_at: the owning block's session, from its outstanding window

params.name: CCV_P_W_REQ_MIU_DCU
params.doc: req_id on MIU -> DCU: correlates a response with its request. Per hop, never shared across hops, and not rob_tag (one instruction can be several transactions; FET has no ROB tag). Sixteen outstanding cache accesses: four slots, four deep, since hits and misses return at different times.
params.decided_at: the owning block's session, from its outstanding window

params.name: CCV_P_W_REQ_DCU_MLC
params.doc: req_id on DCU -> MLC: correlates a response with its request. Per hop, never shared across hops, and not rob_tag (one instruction can be several transactions; FET has no ROB tag). Sixteen fills in flight, i.e. sixteen MSHRs.
params.decided_at: the owning block's session, from its outstanding window

params.name: CCV_P_W_REQ_FET_MLC
params.doc: req_id on FET -> MLC: correlates a response with its request. Per hop, never shared across hops, and not rob_tag (one instruction can be several transactions; FET has no ROB tag). Four instruction fills in flight.
params.decided_at: the owning block's session, from its outstanding window

params.name: CCV_P_W_REQ_MLC_EXB
params.doc: req_id on MLC -> EXB: correlates a response with its request. Per hop, never shared across hops, and not rob_tag (one instruction can be several transactions; FET has no ROB tag). The TL-C source-id width the tilelink_tlc sizing assumed (6 bits), so EXB maps it without translation.
params.decided_at: the owning block's session, from its outstanding window

params.name: CCV_P_W_REQ_MLC_PROBE
params.doc: req_id on MLC -> DCU probe and its acknowledgement: correlates a response with its request. Per hop, never shared across hops, and not rob_tag (one instruction can be several transactions; FET has no ROB tag). Four probes in flight.
params.decided_at: the owning block's session, from its outstanding window

params.name: CCV_P_W_KILL_EPOCH
params.doc: Kill epoch, broadcast with kill_valid and echoed on every kill ack, so a late ack from a previous kill cannot satisfy the next one. One bit suffices while RAU has one kill in flight; two leaves room.
params.decided_at: RAU session, from how many kills may overlap

params.name: CCV_P_W_FETCH_EPOCH
params.doc: Fetch epoch on ccv_ooe_fet_redirect: FET bumps it on a redirect and discards in-flight fetches from the wrong path by epoch.
params.decided_at: FET session, from fetch pipeline depth

params.name: CCV_L_W_CLASS
params.doc: Eight uop classes: integer, float, SFU and convert, memory, control, collective, predicate, spare. DEC decides whether class is derivable from opcode at all.
params.decided_at: DEC block session -- is class derivable from opcode?

params.name: CCV_L_W_OPCODE
params.doc: One encoding across all three hops, owned by the schema (Q-34): a block may narrow it locally only as a strict projection, never a re-encoding. Narrowing at RCU->LANE is likely, but the ISA opcode census sets it. Anything decoding this field will be rewritten.
params.decided_at: ISA opcode census, then DEC/OOE/RCU agree the hops

params.name: CCV_L_W_MEM_OP
params.doc: Architectural memory operation: load, store, atomic family, prefetch, fence.

params.name: CCV_L_W_SPM_OP
params.doc: Scratchpad bank access: read, write, and room for a read-modify variant.

params.name: CCV_L_W_COH_OP
params.doc: Coherent line request: acquire, release, probe response, writeback, grant acknowledgement. Follows the TL-C subset chosen.
params.decided_at: MLC/EXB session, once the TL-C subset is chosen

params.name: CCV_L_W_PROBE_TYPE
params.doc: Kind of inbound message on ccv_exb_mlc_rsp: 0 = a response to a request; otherwise a probe and what it asks (to-invalid, to-branch, to-trunk, after TL-C Probe param). Replaces the one-bit inbound_probe flag.

params.name: CCV_L_W_GRID_SEL
params.doc: Grid selector on the host's kill request (ccv_cru_rau_cfg). RAU maps grid to warp mask from tables it owns. Sized for 256 grid slots; the real number is how many grids RAU tracks at once.

params.name: CCV_L_W_OWNERSHIP
params.doc: TL-C permission levels plus an explicit dirty bit, kept wider than TL-C needs so a CHI bridge maps without a second translation.

params.name: CCV_L_W_SPACE
params.doc: Memory space: global, shared, const, local, with spare codes.

params.name: CCV_L_W_ORDERING
params.doc: Two bits of order and two of scope. Whether scope is a separate field is the open part.
params.decided_at: OOE/MIU session -- is scope a separate field?

params.name: CCV_L_W_ITLB_ENTRY
params.doc: ITLB entry: physical page number, permissions, ASID and valid, rounded up.
params.decided_at: MMU session, with the page-table format

params.name: CCV_L_W_PRF_BASE
params.doc: Physical register window base, at REGISTER granularity. Chunked allocation would narrow this and prf_size together -- one decision for the pair.
params.decided_at: RAU/OOE session -- register or chunk granularity

params.name: CCV_L_W_PRF_SIZE
params.doc: Physical register window size. Same granularity decision as CCV_L_W_PRF_BASE.

params.name: CCV_L_W_PCA_BANK
params.doc: Parked-context bank select: eight banks of four warps, from the proposed PCA organization.
params.decided_at: PCA session, from the parked-array organization

params.name: CCV_L_OPERANDS_PER_LANE
params.doc: Operands shipped to a lane per beat. Whether a lane receives one instruction's operands or several, and whether the destination is read back for accumulate, both change this.
params.decided_at: RCU/LANE session -- see the src_arch vs operand mismatch

params.name: CCV_L_PC_GROUPS
params.doc: PCs carried in one migration, one per PC group. The real count depends on the divergence representation, which is unspecified.

params.name: CCV_L_W_PRED_STATE
params.doc: Predicate registers plus a reconvergence stack of eight entries of mask and PC. THE most likely field to be underestimated: the divergence model is stored here and has never been specified.

params.name: CCV_L_W_BAR_COUNT
params.doc: Barrier entries in an allocated range. 7 bits expresses 1..64; 6 would do with a bias. Not stated by the payload pass, so the biasing choice is still open.
params.decided_at: SYU session -- is the count biased?

params.name: CCV_L_PAGE_SHIFT
params.doc: Page shift, used to express code bounds at page granularity. 4 KB pages assumed; the MMU session confirms.

params.decided_at: EXB session -- flattened bundle or separate TL channels
params.name: CCV_L_W_TL_OUT
params.doc: TL-C outbound, A + C + E plus a valid bit per TL channel, at 512-bit beat, 48-bit address, 6-bit source, 4-bit sink: A 641 (opcode 3, param 3, size 4, source 6, address 48, mask 64, data 512, corrupt 1), C 577 (A without mask), E 4 (sink), valids 3.

params.decided_at: EXB session -- flattened bundle or separate TL channels
params.name: CCV_L_W_TL_IN
params.doc: TL-C inbound, B + D plus a valid bit per TL channel: B 641 (as A), D 533 (opcode 3, param 2, size 4, source 6, sink 4, denied 1, data 512, corrupt 1), valids 2. The earlier single 1760 reproduces exactly as A + C + D + E + 5 valids -- it never included B, the probe.

params.decided_at: CRU session -- the CSR fabric has no topology yet
params.name: CCV_L_W_CSR_ADDR
params.doc: CSR address. A first guess, made only so the common CSR port can be declared: the schema gave csr_req as 'address, write data, write enable' with no widths, and there is no CSR map yet.
